newsitem.title: USA: US W.COAST SPOT PRODUCTS FIRM WITH STRONG MARKETS - AUG 12.
newsitem.headline: US W.COAST SPOT PRODUCTS FIRM WITH STRONG MARKETS - AUG 12.

text.p: Prices for U.S. West Coast refined petroleum products firmed Tuesday, in line with gains in other markets, traders said.
Gasoline spot prices, which reflect what dealers charge at the pipeline, rose about three cents a gallon in California Tuesday to betweem 74 and 75 cents a gallon.
Local markets got a lift from a rally in futures prices, which closed a sharp 2.24 cents a gallon higher on the New York Mercantile Exchange (NYMEX) Tuesday.
Prices also rose after weekly data showed a slight drop in West Coast gasoline inventories, according to the American Petroleum Institute (API).
"It's not a huge draw (on gasoline), but in the current market, it's a bullish signal," a trader said.
Traders struck at least one deal for CARB unleaded gasoline at 73 cents in San Francisco, they said. September shipments of gasoline cost four cents less.
Meanwhile, a major oil company was shipping 200,000 barrel cargo of gasoline from the U.S. Gulf to West Coast, traders said, declining further detail.
State-mandated CARB gasoline prices have risen about seven a cents a gallon since Friday's collapse was prompted panicking sellers.
Conventional unleaded gasoline prices rose three cents for the second straight day to 70/72 cents, while disillates, including diesel and jet fuels, gained about one cent.
